title: A descendant combinator written as a long run of padding stalls the pattern
title_original: Fix inefficient trimming of comments and white space
text_rewritten:
Selectors reaching us from generated CSS sometimes carry a very long run of whitespace, or a long run of comments, between two simple selectors -- the descendant combinator, just written verbosely. Handling one of those takes tens of seconds where the same selector written with a single space takes microseconds, and the cost climbs faster than the length of the padding, so a slightly longer run stops returning at all.

Padding is semantically irrelevant and should cost time proportional to its length. Short padding, padding at the start and end of a pattern, and comments used as padding must all keep resolving to the same selector they resolve to today.
body:
Selectors reaching us from generated CSS sometimes carry a very long run of whitespace, or a long run of comments, between two simple selectors -- the descendant combinator, just written verbosely. Handling one of those takes tens of seconds where the same selector written with a single space takes microseconds, and the cost climbs faster than the length of the padding, so a slightly longer run stops returning at all.

Padding is semantically irrelevant and should cost time proportional to its length. Short padding, padding at the start and end of a pattern, and comments used as padding must all keep resolving to the same selector they resolve to today.
acceptance_hint: A pattern whose descendant combinator is tens of thousands of whitespace characters, or thousands of comments, compiles and selects promptly and resolves to the same selector as the single-space form.
